title: Calling by the names
hookLine: a du'a that uses His names
tomorrow: why does the Fatiha stop talking about Him and start talking to Him?

lines: OLD, AND NO ONE TO HAND IT ON TO.
cards: Some messages only get typed after midnight, the ones too honest for daylight. Zakariya's prayer was like that. The Qur'an says he cried to his Lord in secret.
He was old. His bones had grown weak, his hair had gone white, his wife had never had a child, and he served in the house of prayer with no one to hand it on to. He had asked before, and kept asking.
Now, in the dark, he asks once more for an heir. And the Qur'an keeps the exact Name he chooses.

teach.b: In Pickthall's words: "My Lord! Leave me not childless, though Thou art the best of inheritors." Look at what he's done.

teach.h: NAME THE NEED, AND LET GO.
teach.b: He asks for an heir, and he calls God by the Name of the One who inherits everything. Al-Warith, from days ago. It works both ways at once.
It names the need: I want someone to carry this on. And it lets go: even if no son comes, You are the best heir of all. The Qur'an says his prayer was heard, and he was given a son, Yahya.
That's the thing to tell a friend tonight: Zakariya asked for an heir by calling God the best of inheritors. The prophets do this again and again.
Ayyub, worn down by suffering, calls on Him as the most merciful of all who show mercy. The Name fits the wound.
And the Qur'an makes it an invitation for everyone, in Surah al-A'raf: "Allah's are the fairest names. Invoke Him by them."
So the ninety-nine aren't a list to memorize and file away. Each one is a way of saying, here's what I need, and here's who I know You to be.

how: Muslims often open or close a du'a with Names suited to the request, Ya Ghafur when asking forgiveness, Ya Razzaq for provision, following 7:180 and the prophets' du'as in the Qur'an.

games.q: what does “calling by the names” mean?
o: asking Allah through the Name that fits the need
repeating all ninety-nine Names in a fixed order
calling on prophets by name to pray for you

games.q: the Name fits the need — tap the pairs.
p: most merciful of all who show mercy

s: saying the right Name guarantees the du'a is answered exactly as asked
the Names aren't passwords. Zakariya's own du'a lets go: You are the best of inheritors either way.
Zakariya called on Allah as the best of inheritors while asking for an heir
"Leave me not childless, though Thou art the best of inheritors."

games.q: you're Zakariya: old, your wife has never had a child, and you've asked before. tonight, in secret, you ask again. what do you say?
o: My Lord, leave me not childless, though You are the best of inheritors.
nothing; at this age asking again is no longer reasonable.
ask only for patience, and stop asking for a child at all.
games.why: he asks once more, and names God as the best of inheritors. the Qur'an says his prayer was heard, and Yahya was born.

practice: If you pray, choose three Names that fit what you need today, and call on Him by them in your own words, the way Zakariya did. If not, say three things you need out loud, plainly, and sit with what you said.

wordCard.voice: Calling by the names: asking Allah through the Name that fits the need, as the prophets did.

orig.note: Arabic: the best of inheritors, Zakariya's Name for Allah in 21:89.

carryVoice: The line to keep: call him by name, the one that fits tonight's need. That's the Names, gathered.

sources.q: My Lord! Leave me not childless, though Thou art the best of inheritors.
Allah's are the fairest names. Invoke Him by them.

sources.ref: Qur'an 19:2–9 (Zakariya's secret cry: old age, white hair, a barren wife) and 21:90 (his prayer heard; Yahya given)
Qur'an 21:83 (Ayyub: most merciful of all who show mercy)
